publisher_assessment.decision: LEĠIŻLAZZJONI MALTA is accepted as Malta’s official legislation publisher within each reviewed record; Identità, Missions Malta, Legal Aid Malta, IDPC, the Office of the Ombudsman and Judiciary Malta are accepted only for named official pages and service scopes. EUR-Lex is accepted as the official EU legal and case-law reference publisher for the listed records.
publisher_assessment.basis: The official S.L. 217.04 English PDF reviewed on 2026-10-21 identifies amendments through Legal Notices 183 and 204 of 2026. Identità’s current EU-family parent page links July 2026 Forms F.01 and F.02 and a foreign-document policy page displaying Version 2.0. Current official Identità pages identify the EU-family application route, while the C-visa FAQ distinguishes the Ministry’s Type C role from Identità’s Type D role. The Administrative Justice Act record displays an in-force record published 2026-09-25; the Code of Organization and Civil Procedure point-in-time text is dated 2026-10-01. The EU residence-card dependency register now includes Regulation 2025/1208 and CJEU C-61/22.
publisher_assessment.limits: The accepted links do not establish that Malta’s legal topics are adequately covered or that all displayed guidance is legally correct. In particular, Identità family-category wording and EEA/Maltese route descriptions need comparison with the national instruments and Directive 2004/38. Visa-representation, FOI/IDPC and card-specimen currentness remain open. No local copy or topic is accepted.
publisher_assessment.local_copy_and_reuse: No local source copies are accepted in the published pack. Article 13 of the Statute Law Revision Act, 2021 (Act XL of 2021) restricts reproducing revised editions without Government permission; its publication exception excludes reproductions based on scans or electronic reproductions of the revised edition. The statutory copies previously captured were derived from official revised-edition PDFs, and no permission was obtained. Item-specific republication terms were not established for captured guidance pages and forms. Only scoped official links remain as public source references.

policy: For ordinary source use, a trustworthy government-published consolidation or clearly identified official guidance, form, service or EU legal source may be used as an external reference within its displayed identity, status, version, language, date and scope.
